key_insight: Picard–Chebyshev weakly nonlinear analysis predicts streak-breakdown triggers by tracking interactions that generate oblique and harmonic waves with alternating streamwise vortices.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support transition prediction by identifying finite-amplitude disturbances that destabilize otherwise laminar channel flow.
method: Formulate weakly nonlinear optimal perturbation analysis for compressible parallel flows using Picard–Chebyshev iteration.
Track non-modal amplification and nonlinear interactions across an expanding set of wavenumber components.
Progress from linear dynamics to weakly nonlinear amplitude equations and higher-order approximations.
evidence_signal: For subcritical plane Poiseuille flow at Mach 0.3 and Reynolds number 3000, the abstract reports high agreement with DNS and identifies a planar-wave perturbation that triggers streak breakdown in full nonlinear simulation.
watch_item: Demonstrated accuracy is limited to the reported flow conditions and weakly nonlinear regime; the expanding wavenumber set may increase computational cost.
paper_title: Predicting trigger in streak breakdown via Picard-Chebyshev approach in plane-Poiseuille flow
